method: Thread pairs and rows are parsed as strict whole numbers, limited to 2-6 pairs and 4-40 rows. Each pair has one six-digit hex color and supplies two mirrored strands, so the starting order is A through the final pair label followed by the same labels in reverse. Rows cycle through pair colors from the outermost pair toward the center and then repeat. Every row uses the current outer pair as the working strands: pairs minus one forward knots on the left, pairs minus one backward knots on the right and one joining knot at the center, for 2 × pairs − 1 knots per row. Total knots are rows × knots per row; per-color totals count the rows assigned to each pair. The preview places each row's knots in a V and colors them by the working pair. This is a symbolic chevron layout and tying sequence, not a thread-length, bracelet-size or tension estimate. It accepts no files, stores nothing and transmits nothing.
